content.comment_body: I was able to read and write inputs, outputs, and flags using libnodave, but is it possible to access and modify blocks, such as timer values? For example, if you have a multifunction switch with parameters for off delay time or permanent light, can you set or get different values from the [product_name]?

Hello, Set up the configuration so you can write to the controller at DB1VB100. Then, in [product_name] software, start the online test, open the data table, and add VB100. Now, you should see the value coming in from libnodave. This confirms you can transfer data between libnodave and [product_name]. To adjust parameters as mentioned before, use the VM-mapping table in the [product_name] software, select the function block needed, and choose the parameter of the function block you want to change. Parameters you can change or just view are indicated in the VM-mapping table. Alternatively, you can read the VM-address in the program via NAI, use an analog function block, and then reference it to handle the value accordingly. Hope you find this helpful.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are seeking advanced methods to exchange data between external libraries and [product_name] controllers, aiming to manipulate internal function block parameters like timer values rather than just basic I/O. There is some uncertainty around proper mapping and access to deeper memory regions and parameters, which can impact usability and flexibility for those requiring beyond-standard control capabilities.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to have the ability to directly access and change internal block parameters, such as timer values, in the [product_name] controller using external tools like libnodave, in a way similar to manipulating standard I/O or flags.
